english.title: Receiver / manager fail to deliver accounts to registrar
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a

(A)_[receiver]_
(B)_[manager]_

of the property of a company, namely **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..), who had been appointed under powers contained in an instrument, namely **(..SPECIFY POWERS OF APPOINTMENT..), failed to deliver to the registrar of companies for registration the requisite accounts of your receipts and payments within the prescribed period as set out in section 38(2) of the Insolvency Act 1986 and as an abstract in the prescribed form showing receipts and payments as set out in section 38(3) of that Act
english.legislation: Contrary to section 38 of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.

english.notes: (i) Section 431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 provides that notwithstanding anything in section 127(1) of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980, an information relating to such an offence which is triable by a magistrates' court in England and Wales may be so tried if it is laid at any time within 3 years after the commission of the offence and within 12 months after the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Secretary of State (as the case may be) to justify the proceedings comes to his knowledge. Summary proceedings in Scotland for such an offence shall not be commenced after the expiration of 3 years from the commission of the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding one-fifth of statutory maximum or on a second or subsequent conviction to a fine not exceeding one-fiftieth of the statutory maximum for each day on which the contravention is continued.
